title: fix(core): the id_field no-declared-twin diagnostic carries the spec's published FIELD_KEY_GUIDANCE reason (objectui#7650)
body:
Fixes #7650
Clause-②: no — a dev-mode diagnostic's text now comes from the spec's published guidance; no accepted document, published type or served value changes. The PR still waits as a draft for the director seat's review.

The one open slice of objectui#7650, `id_field`, as claimed in comment 5904884226. ⚠️ This stays a DRAFT for the director seat's contract review, per the maintainer's instruction of 2026-09-29 quoted in the dispatch. The dev does not mark it ready and does not enable auto-merge.

Implemented in session `https://claude.ai/code/session_012UwY3ahMixEFkfTUxMVkYm` (PM seat `domain:spec @ objectui`, dispatched dev).

## What changes

In `packages/core/src/utils/reference-keys.ts`, `warnUnfoldableRetiredKey` now appends `FIELD_KEY_GUIDANCE.id_field.why` to the dev-mode line when the refusal is `no-declared-twin` and the authored key is exactly `id_field`. `FIELD_KEY_GUIDANCE` is imported from `@objectstack/spec/data`, next to the `FieldSchema` import the module already had.

- ⛔ No local copy of the spec's prose, and no optional read with a fallback. These are the two refusals the module comment recorded, and neither one moves. The read is the bare expression `FIELD_KEY_GUIDANCE.id_field.why`, with no `?.` and no `??`. It sits after the `isDev()` and memo checks, so production never evaluates it. On a spec without the row it throws in dev, before the memo is taken, instead of warning with less.
- ⛔ The fold does not change. `canonicalizeRetiredFieldKeys` is not touched, `id_field` is never folded, and no `idField` read is added. `lintAuthoredRecordKeys` is not called and no near match is offered. The appended text is the contract's own sentence about the key. A typo (`sortible`) gets neither a suggestion nor the `id_field` reason.
- Only the exact spelling gets the reason. The spec keys that row in snake_case on purpose: a `why` row matches only the exact authored spelling, with no alias probe. The diagnostic follows the same rule.
- Module comment: the paragraph that called the slice 「NOT TAKEN」 now says what the code does, under the heading `id_field: never folded, and the diagnostic carries the spec's own reason`. The `no-declared-twin` bullet in the `warnUnfoldableRetiredKey` docblock gets one matching sentence.
- Changeset `.changeset/7650-id-field-published-guidance.md` bumps `@object-ui/core` as a `patch`. There is no floor raise (see premise 2).

## Premises, re-measured on `origin/main` `0ffc423b1` before writing

1. **Installed row.** `packages/core/node_modules/@objectstack/spec/package.json` reads `17.5.0`. `FIELD_KEY_GUIDANCE` is exported from the `@objectstack/spec/data` entry and typed as a readonly record of `{ to?: string; why?: string }`. Its `id_field` row has one key, `why`: a `why` and no `to`. Lit control in the same read: the `startingNumber` row is present with a `why`. Dark control: in the npm-packed `17.4.0` tarball, `dist/data/index.mjs` has 0 hits for `id_field` and 2 for `startingNumber`. npm lists no version between 17.4.0 and 17.5.0.
2. **Consumer floor.** `@object-ui/core` already declares `"@objectstack/spec": "^17.5.0"` (raised by PR objectui#11086). No raise was needed, so the lockfile is unchanged. `check:spec-floors`, run after building core, reports no finding for `@object-ui/core` and 0 `floor-too-low` findings overall. The gate's exit 1 comes from 18 `no-artifact` findings, all for packages not built in this worktree. That is a missing prerequisite, so those 18 are NOT MEASURED; it is not a red.
3. **Before reading**, taken through the real exported `normalizeSchemaReferenceKeys` (source module, `node --experimental-strip-types`). The `id_field` line went straight from "...and this path deliberately does not guess a near match." to "The key and its value are LEFT on the def exactly as served...", with no spec reason. After the change, the same line has "`@objectstack/spec`'s `FIELD_KEY_GUIDANCE` gives the reason: " plus the installed row's `why` between those two sentences. The `sortible` and `startingNumber` lines from the same probe are unchanged.
4. ⚠️ **This premise is partly false.** `ExpressionProvider.tsx` and `RecordFormPage.tsx` mention `FIELD_KEY_GUIDANCE` only in comments. Nothing in the tree imports it: `git grep` for an import of the symbol finds 0 hits, against a lit control of 192 files that import from `@objectstack/spec/data`. So the import follows this module's own `FieldSchema` import from the same subpath.

## Tests

The new describe `the id_field diagnostic carries the PUBLISHED spec reason (objectui#7650)` is in `reference-keys.retiredDialect-7650.test.ts`. Every read of the row happens at test time and is unconditional. The test holds no copy of the prose.

- `the installed row is a retirement — a why, and no to`
- `the no-declared-twin line for id_field carries that why, and the key is still not folded`
- `the reason is read off the spec module when the line is built — not from a copy`: substitutes the row through `vi.doMock` with `importOriginal`
- `a spec WITHOUT the row fails loudly in dev instead of warning with less, and production never reads it`: removes the row through `vi.doMock`; the production leg is the control
- `a TYPO still gets no suggestion — and not the id_field reason either`

(The backticks around the key names inside those test names are dropped here.) Two sentences in the same file were corrected because this change made them false: the header bullet that said the row "is in NO published version", and the title of the `id_field` negative pin, which said "the slice is blocked on a spec release". That pin is now titled `does NOT fold id_field — no declared successor`.

## Ablations: each from committed HEAD `21306be7b`, with the direction predicted before the run

Each leg ran through `ablation-replace.mjs`. The anchor must hit exactly once, and the tool checks the on-disk anchor and replacement counts and the blob change. Each leg ran under a `trap` restore on EXIT INT TERM and was restored by state: the blob is back to the HEAD blob `8347e30f9e83`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty. No build was needed: the tests import `../reference-keys` by relative path (source), and the mocked module is the unchanged spec dist.

| leg | mutation | predicted | observed (4 reference-keys files, 77 tests) |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | drop the reason from the line: `${detail}${published}` becomes `${detail}` | 2 red: the "carries that why" pin and the substitution pin | 2 failed / 75 passed, exactly those two |
| M2 | optional read with a local fallback: `?.why ?? 'LOCAL FALLBACK SENTENCE'` | 1 red: the row-absent pin | 1 failed / 76 passed, exactly that pin |
| M3 | local copy: the read replaced by the installed sentence as a literal | 2 red: the substitution pin and the row-absent pin; the "carries that why" pin stays GREEN, because a copy satisfies it | 2 failed / 75 passed, exactly those two |
| M4 | the reason widened to every `no-declared-twin` key | 1 red: the typo pin | 1 failed / 76 passed, exactly that pin |

⚠️ The first M4 attempt was a no-op: the tool refused it before running anything, because the replacement was a substring of the anchor and so its count could not rise. It is not a measurement. M4 in the table is the re-run with a replacement that is not inside the anchor.

## Acceptance notes

1. ⚠️ **Finding, not fixed here.** For `id_field` (and for `title_format`), the diagnostic's shared closing clause is not true today. It reads: "the consumers read only the spelling `@objectstack/spec`'s `FieldSchema` declares, so this value reaches no reader". There are production reads of both snake spellings. In `packages/plugin-charts/src/ObjectChart.tsx`, the expression `fieldDef.id_field || 'id'` reads it, and its own census comment traces that def to `getObjectSchema`. In `packages/app-shell/src/utils/resolveActionParams.ts`, `idField: field.id_field` and `titleFormat: field.title_format` read them. The clause came with objectui#8938 and this PR does not change it, but it now sits on the same line as the spec's reason. The diagnostic text has not been released yet: the changeset `8938-retired-dialect-measured-surface.md` is still pending, and `@object-ui/core@17.6.0` on npm contains none of that text. So the clause would ship as-is in the next release. Fixing it means deciding who the readers are, or retiring those two reads, which the spec's reason argues for. That is a judgement for the reviewing seat, so it is reported to the seat and not filed by this dev.
2. **Observation, not filed.** Other `FIELD_KEY_GUIDANCE` rows that carry a `why` (for example `startingNumber`) also land in the `no-declared-twin` arm, and they get no reason. They are outside this slice under both the claim's file surface and the no-optional-read rule. Generalising would need its own ruling on what the line says when a row is absent.

## 维护者速读(草稿)

- **改了什么**:对象里存着旧键 `id_field` 时，开发模式下的那条诊断现在会带上 spec 官方写的理由（`FIELD_KEY_GUIDANCE.id_field.why`，直接读已安装的 spec，本仓不存副本）。
- **没改什么**：`id_field` 仍然不会被折叠成别的键；生产环境行为、服务出去的数据、公开类型都不变。
- **风险**:spec 若缺了这一行，开发模式直接报错而不是悄悄少说一句（这是卡上两条拒绝的要求）；依赖下限 `^17.5.0` 已经保证有这一行。回滚就是撤这个 PR。
- **席位意见**:（留空，待总监席契约复审）
- **你要做的**：无；等总监席复审。另有一条发现（诊断末句「没有读者」对 `id_field` 不成立）交席位判断。


## Round 2: the closing clause no longer claims that no reader sees the value

In response to the seat's ACCEPT comment 5905375580 on objectui#7650. Head `a71744d4f`. Only words change. No read, no fold and no `id_field` reason logic changes, and the one code line that changes is the message string.

- **Why.** The line ended on "so this value reaches no reader". That is false where a retired spelling is still read on purpose. `resolveActionParam` (`@object-ui/app-shell`) reads `idField: field.id_field` and `titleFormat: field.title_format`. objectui#7435 kept those reads, and its pin `resolveActionParams.declaredLookupLegs-7435.test.ts` calls them "the snake spellings that must keep working". `resolveGroupByLabels` (`@object-ui/plugin-charts`) reads `fieldDef.id_field || 'id'`.
- **Diagnostic.** The closing clause is shared by all three refusals. It now reads: "but a consumer that reads only the spellings `@objectstack/spec`'s `FieldSchema` declares will not see this value."
- **Docblock.** In the `warnUnfoldableRetiredKey` docblock, "a key that does not fold reaches none of them" and "a value nothing reads" now apply only to the consumers of the declared spellings. A new paragraph names the kept readers by symbol (`resolveActionParam`, `resolveGroupByLabels`). It says the list is not complete (`deriveColumns` in `@object-ui/plugin-form` also reads `display_field`) and that nothing re-derives a complete list. Two other sentences in the same file made the same claim and are narrowed the same way: the module docblock's "the consumers … read none of it", and the `canonical-occupied` bullet's "the retired one is inert". The `canonical-occupied` comment in the 7650 pin file ("reaches no consumer") is narrowed the same way too.
- **Pending changeset `8938-retired-dialect-measured-surface.md`.** One dated correction note is appended at the end, under the maintainer's ruling 「Allow the appended note (Recommended)」. `git diff` of that file shows 11 additions and 0 deletions. Its first 39 lines (2491 bytes, frontmatter included) are byte-identical to the base. The note also corrects that file's "the retired value is inert", which makes the same claim for the occupied case. `check-changeset-overwrite` lists the file as a modified pre-existing changeset (exit 0). The declaration is unchanged: `@object-ui/core: minor` before and after.
- **This PR's own changeset** gets one sentence about the correction.

**Pins.** Two new tests in the same describe:
- `the id_field line never claims NO reader sees the value — kept snake reads do`: the line does not contain "reaches no reader". As a lit control on the same line, it still carries the narrower claim.
- `CONTROL — the scoped claim is kept where it is true, beside the fact it states`: an occupied `displayField` that keeps the producer's value, plus a typo. Both lines carry "will not see this value".

(The backticks in the first test name are dropped here.)

**Ablation**, from committed HEAD `a71744d4f`: the old two-line clause was restored through `ablation-replace.mjs`. The anchor went from 1 hit to 0 and the blob from `5cc832c5b346` to `e0eaee263d61`. "reaches no reader" counts 1 in the mutated file and 0 at HEAD. The prediction was 2 red, the two new pins. The run gave `Tests 2 failed | 77 passed (79)`, and the two failures were exactly those pins. The file was restored and checked by state: the blob is back to `5cc832c5b346` and `git diff HEAD` is empty. A trap on EXIT INT TERM guarded the restore.

**Gates at `a71744d4f`** (exit codes captured before any pipe):
- `pnpm --filter "@object-ui/core^..." build` then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core type-check`: 0. `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core lint`: 0, with 0 errors. The 568 warnings were already there, and the two touched source files have 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- The four reference-keys files: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 79 passed (79)`. `packages/core/`: `Test Files 190 passed (190)`, `Tests 3739 passed | 27 skipped (3766)`. The 21 outside files: `Test Files 21 passed (21)`, `Tests 192 passed (192)`.
- Exit 0: check-changeset-presence, check-changeset-claims, check-changeset-fixed, check-changeset-no-major, check-changeset-overwrite (it reports the appended 8938 changeset as its case 2, a deliberate correction), check:pending-changeset-literals, check:control-bytes, check:new-line-citations (0 new). `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on the four paths: NOT GOVERNED.

**Noted, not changed.** A test title in `reference-keys.measuredSurface-8938.test.ts`, `speaks up when the canonical key is OCCUPIED — the retired value is inert, and that was silent`, makes the same "inert" claim. That file is outside the claim's file surface, so it is left for the seat.

The `Clause-②: no` declaration above still holds, because only text changes.
